evidence.title: Combustion Analysis of a CI Engine with Biodiesel Blends based on Vibro-Acoustic Measurement
evidence.abstract: In this paper, a combustion analysis of a compression ignition (CI) engine operating with biodiesel blends has been experimentally investigated to examine the effects of biodiesel on the combustion process and the characteristics of the engine noise produced by the combustion process. The experiment with different loads and speeds was conducted on a four-cylinder, four-stroke, direct injection and turbocharged diesel engine fuelled with biodiesel (B50 and B100) and normal pure diesel. The signals of vibration, acoustic and the in-cylinder pressure were measured for analysing the engine combustion. In order to examine these signals, a coherent power spectrum analysis method is used to investigate the engine noise signals for locating the frequency band which is closely related to the combustion process. Subsequently, the Wigner-Ville distribution is employed to analyse the energy distribution of engine noise in the time-frequency domain. A band-pass filter based on fractional Fourier transform is developed to extract the main combustion induced noise from the engine noise for comparison. The interim results show that the sound energy level of combustion noise of engine fuelled by biodiesel and its blends is higher than that of engine fuelled by diesel. This is also identical to the variation of in-cylinder pressure. Hence, acoustic signals of the CI engine provide useful features for remote engine condition monitoring and supply fuel monitoring

evidence.title: Investigating the Effect of Engine Lubricant Viscosity on Engine Friction and Fuel Economy of a Diesel Engine
evidence.abstract:
Fuel economy is affected, both by fuel and engine lubricant quality. Engine lubricant quality plays a vital role in reduction of fuel consumption by effective reduction of friction between the contact surfaces of engine parts (piston ring assembly, bearings and valve train). Engine components are exposed to various lubrication regimes such as hydrodynamic, elasto-hydrodynamic, boundary and mixed lubrication during engine operation. In each of these regimes, the factors which influence engine friction are different. Hydrodynamic friction is influenced by lubricant rheology, film thickness and sliding speed of interacting surfaces, whereas boundary and elasto-hydrodynamic friction is a function of surface properties like roughness and hardness and the type of friction modifier used in engine lubricant. So the principal factors which influence engine friction power are speed, load, and surface topography of engine components, oil viscosity, oil temperature and type of friction modifiers used.



It is generally accepted that both the piston assembly and bearings are predominantly in the hydrodynamic lubrication regime, whereas the valve train is in the mixed/boundary lubrication regime. Hydrodynamic friction is proportional to sliding velocity of a pair, oil film thickness, operating temperature, lubricant viscosity and many other physical parameters.

mechanism_map.mechanism: Combustion-induced engine noise can be characterized and isolated from overall engine noise via vibro-acoustic signal processing (vibration, acoustic, in-cylinder pressure) combined with coherent power spectrum analysis and time-frequency methods (Wigner-Ville distribution), which identify the dominant frequency band linked to the combustion process.
mechanism_map.intervention: Mount a triaxial accelerometer on the 2021 Toyota RAV4 engine block and a microphone near the engine bay, record the grinding noise with the vehicle stationary under repeated no-load run conditions, and process the signals using coherent power spectrum analysis followed by Wigner-Ville distribution to determine whether the dominant energy lies in a combustion-related band or in a mechanical/auxiliary band.
mechanism_map.expected_effect: If the grinding noise's spectral energy concentrates in a frequency band coherent with cylinder pressure (combustion-related), the noise source is the combustion process (e.g., abnormal combustion/misfire); if the energy falls outside combustion bands, the source is mechanical (e.g., bearing, accessory drive, water pump, starter/flywheel gear), which is consistent with the absence of a warning light and with battery replacement not resolving the issue.
mechanism_map.falsification_test: Repeat the measurement on a known-good 2021 RAV4 at the same stationary no-load conditions and compare the time-frequency energy distribution; if the grinding-noise spectrum does not share the same dominant frequency band and coherence with in-cylinder pressure as the reference vehicle, the combustion-noise mechanism is falsified and a mechanical source should be investigated instead.

candidates.intervention: Re-specify the engine lubricant fill for the 2021 Toyota RAV4 to a higher-viscosity SAE grade (e.g., move from 0W-16 to 5W-30) of the same API performance category, ensuring hydrodynamic film thickness on the piston assembly and bearings while supplying the valvetrain in the mixed/boundary regime with adequate additive-derived boundary protection.

evidence_bundle.mechanism_source_span: Engine lubricant quality plays a vital role in reduction of fuel consumption by effective reduction of friction between the contact surfaces of engine parts (piston ring assembly, bearings and valve train). Engine components are exposed to various lubrication regimes such as hydrodynamic, elasto-hydrodynamic, boundary and mixed lubrication during engine operation. In each of these regimes, the factors which influence engine friction are different. Hydrodynamic friction is influenced by lubricant rheology, film thickness and sliding speed of interacting surfaces, whereas boundary and elasto-hydrodynamic friction is a function of surface properties like roughness and hardness and the type of friction modifier used in engine lubricant. So the principal factors which influence engine friction power are speed, load, and surface topography of engine components, oil viscosity, oil temperature and type of friction modifiers used.

cemetery_warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

The experiment with different loads and speeds was conducted on a four-cylinder, four-stroke, direct injection and turbocharged diesel engine fuelled with biodiesel (B50 and B100) and normal pure diesel. The signals of vibration, acoustic and the in-cylinder pressure were measured for analysing the engine combustion. In order to examine these signals, a coherent power spectrum analysis method is used to investigate the engine noise signals for locating the frequency band which is closely related to the combustion process. Subsequently, the Wigner-Ville distribution is employed to analyse the energy distribution of engine noise in the time-frequency domain. A band-pass filter based on fractional Fourier transform is developed to extract the main combustion induced noise from the engine noise for comparison. The interim results show that the sound energy level of combustion noise of engine fuelled by biodiesel and its blends is higher than that of engine fuelled by diesel. This is also identical to the variation of in-cylinder pressure. Hence, acoustic signals of the CI engine provide useful features for remote engine condition monitoring and supply fuel monitoring

Fuel economy is affected, both by fuel and engine lubricant quality. Engine lubricant quality plays a vital role in reduction of fuel consumption by effective reduction of friction between the contact surfaces of engine parts (piston ring assembly, bearings and valve train). Engine components are exposed to various lubrication regimes such as hydrodynamic, elasto-hydrodynamic, boundary and mixed lubrication during engine operation. In each of these regimes, the factors which influence engine friction are different. Hydrodynamic friction is influenced by lubricant rheology, film thickness and sliding speed of interacting surfaces, whereas boundary and elasto-hydrodynamic friction is a function of surface properties like roughness and hardness and the type of friction modifier used in engine lubricant. So the principal factors which influence engine friction power are speed, load, and surface topography of engine components, oil viscosity, oil temperature and type of friction modifiers used.



It is generally accepted that both the piston assembly and bearings are predominantly in the hydrodynamic lubrication regime, whereas the valve train is in the mixed/boundary lubrication regime. Hydrodynamic friction is proportional to sliding velocity of a pair, oil film thickness, operating temperature, lubricant viscosity and many other physical parameters.
